name: City Council Adjourned Meeting of June 16, 2021
minutes_text:
APPROVAL OF MINUTES
  EL MONTE CITY COUNCIL REGULAR MEETING
  OF JUNE 16, 2021

MEETING JOINTLY AND REGULARLY WITH THE EL MONTE HOUSING AUTHORITY; EL
MONTE PUBLIC FINANCING AUTHORITY; EL MONTE WATER AUTHORITY; EL MONTE
PARKING AUTHORITY; SUCCESSOR AGENCY TO THE FORMER EL MONTE COMMUNITY
REDEVELOPMENT AGENCY; HOUSING SUCCESSOR AGENCY; AND, FROM TIME TO
TIME, SUCH OTHER BODIES OF THE CITY WHOSE MEMBERSHIP IS COMPOSED
EXCLUSIVELY OF THE MEMBERSHIP OF THE CITY COUNCIL

1.  CALL TO ORDER: 6:00 p.m.

2.  ROLL CALL FOR CITY COUNCIL AND AUTHORITY BODIES:

  Jessica Ancona, Mayor/Chair – present (via zoom)
  Victoria Martinez Muela, Mayor Pro Tem/Authority Member – present
  Martin R. Herrera, Councilmember/Authority Member – present
  Dr. Maria Morales, Councilmember/Authority Member – present
  Alma D. Puente, Councilmember/Authority Member – present

3.  APPROVAL OF AGENDA:

  WITH THE FOLLOWING EDITS/CHANGES TO THE AGENDA:

  Item 14.3 has been pulled.

  m) Dr. Morales
  s) Councilmember Herrera  4-1 (Mayor Pro Tem Martinez Muela No)

4.  CLOSED SESSION:

  The City Council and the various Authority Bodies whose membership is composed
  exclusively of the membership of the City Council (collectively, the “Council”) will attempt
  to address and complete all Closed Session business between 6:00 p.m. and 7:00 p.m.
  If the Council completes all Closed Session business prior to 7:00 p.m., the Council will
  take a short recess and commence all Open Session proceedings promptly at 7:00 p.m.
  In the event the City Council is unable to address or complete all agendized Closed
  Session items by 7:00 p.m., the Council will hear all such remaining items toward the end
  of the meeting, immediately following Council Communications. Should any member of
  the public wish to address the Council on any agendized Closed Session matter, the
  Council shall allow such person to address the Council on such matter prior to going into
  Closed Session, provided that all persons wishing to address the Council on an agendized
  Closed Session matter shall fill out a speaker card and be subject to a speaker’s time limit
  of 3 minutes per speaker and further provided that the Council shall be under no obligation
  to respond to or deliberate upon any specific questions or comments posed by a speaker
  or take action on any issue raised by a speaker beyond such action as the City Council
   City Council Meeting Minutes of June 16, 2021

may be lawfully authorized to take on an agendized Closed Session matter pursuant to
the Brown Act (Govt. Code Section 54950 et seq.).

Mayor Pro Tem Martinez Muela invited members of the public to address the City
Council on Closed Session Items 4.1 through 4.4.

Mayor Pro Tem Martinez Muela and the City Council recessed into Closed Session
at approximately 6:04 p.m. Mayor Ancona and the City Council reconvened from
Closed Session at approximately 7:33 p.m.

Assistant City Attorney Richard Padilla reported out of Closed Session with respect
to Items 4.1 through 4.4.

4.1  Closed Session Pursuant to Government Code Section 54956.9(d)(2) and (e)(1) –
  Significant Exposure of Litigation – One (1) Potential Case.

  An update was provided by Deputy City Attorney Joaquin Vazquez,
  questions posed by the City Council direction was given but ultimately no
  final action was taken.

4.2  Closed Session Pursuant to Government Code Section 54956.9(d)(1) –
  Conference with Legal Counsel – Existing Litigation Regarding the Following
  Related Matter: Gateway Four, LP; Gateway Two, LP; Gateway Five, LLC, US
  Bankruptcy Court Central District, Lead Case No. 1:20-bk-11581-MB.

  Presentation was given by special legal counsel Zev Chuckman and Mr.
  Vazquez, again direction given by the City Council but no final action taken.

4.3  Closed Session Pursuant to Government Code Section 54956.9(d)(4) –
  Anticipated Litigation – One (1) Matter.

  Discussion was had with City Attorney Rick Olivarez, myself, and Joaquin
  Vazquez and members of the Council, direction was given in closed session
  and no final action taken.

4.4  Closed Session Pursuant to Government Code Section 54956.9(d)(1) –
  Conference with Legal Counsel – Existing Litigation: FEAH, LLC vs. City of El
  Monte, LASC Case No. 20STCP03720.

  Discussion was had in closed session, presentation by Joaquin Vazquez,
  direction given by the City Council in closed session but no final action
  taken.

  2
   City Council Meeting Minutes of June 16, 2021

  OPEN SESSION PROCEEDINGS

(Commencing at 7:00 p.m. or as soon thereafter as the City Council reconvene from Closed
Session/Short Recess).

5.  INVOCATION:  Chaplain Bill Young, Non-Denominational. Present.

6.  FLAG SALUTE:  City Council. Councilmember Puente.

7.  RECOGNITIONS, HONORS AND COMMUNITY INTEREST PRESENTATIONS:

  7.1  Presentation by the City Council Proclaiming the Month of June 2021 as National
  Immigrant Heritage Month.

  7.2  Presentation by the City Council Proclaiming June 20-26, 2021 as National
  Mosquito Control Awareness Month. Mr. Jerry Velasco Present.

8.  PUBLIC COMMENT REGARDING NON-AGENDIZED MATTERS:

  This time has been set aside for persons in the audience to make comments or inquiries
  on matters within the general subject matter jurisdiction of the City Council, the Housing
  Authority, the Financing Authority and/or the Water Authority (collectively, the “Council”)
  that are not listed on this agenda. Although no person is required to provide their name
  and address as a condition to attending a Council meeting, persons who wish to address
  the Council are asked to state their name and address. Each speaker will be limited to
  three (3) continuous minutes. Speakers may not lend any portion of their speaking time to
  other persons or borrow additional time from other persons.

  Except as otherwise provided under the Brown Act (Gov. Code Section 54950 et seq.),
  the Council may not deliberate or take action upon any matter not listed on this posted
  agenda but may order that any such matter be placed on the agenda for a subsequent
  meeting. The Council may also direct staff to investigate certain matters for consideration
  at a future meeting.

  All comments or queries presented by a speaker shall be addressed to the Council as a
  body and not to any specific member thereof. No questions shall be posed to any member
  of the Council except through the presiding official of the meeting, the Mayor and/or Chair.
  Members of the Council are under no obligation to respond to questions posed by
  speakers but may provide brief clarifying responses to any comment made or questions
  posed. The Council may not engage in any sort of prolonged discussion or deliberation
  with any speaker or group of speakers on matters that are not listed on this agenda.

  Enforcement of Decorum: The Chief of Police, or such member, or members of the Police
  Department as the Chief of Police may designate, shall serve as the Sergeant-at-Arms of
  any Council meeting. The Sergeant-at-Arms shall carry out all orders and instructions
  given by the presiding official for the purpose of maintaining order and decorum at the

  3
   City Council Meeting Minutes of June 16, 2021

meeting. While members of the public are free to level criticism of City policies and the
action(s) or proposed action(s) of the Council or its members, members of the public may
not engage in behavior that is disruptive to the orderly conduct of the proceedings,
including, but not limited to, conduct that prevents other members of the public from being
heard when it is their opportunity to speak or which prevents members of the audience
from hearing or seeing the proceedings. Members of the public may not threaten any
person with physical harm or act in a manner that may reasonably be interpreted as an
imminent threat of physical harm. All persons attending the meeting must adhere to the
City’s policy barring harassment based upon a person’s race, religious creed, color,
national origin, ancestry, physical handicap, medical condition, marital status, gender,
sexual orientation or age.

Eddie Batres – I am writing to you in regards to Chief David Reynoso. It was brought to
my attention that Reynoso worked part-time at AIS Security, 4255 Tyler, which is near my
house. This position was authorized by the City Manager. My handicapped friends and I
are very aware of handicapped parking locations that are frequently violated. We take
preventative actions to stop these violations from occurring for obvious reasons. Prior to
Reynoso leaving AIS, my friends noticed that Reynoso routinely parked an EMPD staff
car, license plate #149225, in the only handicapped parking stall on the AIS property. His
vehicle was not equipped with a handicapped license plate nor a placard. The only time
he did not park in the handicapped parking spot was when other employees beat him to
the spot. I have numerous photos which prove my point. Reynoso is the Chief of Police.
Optics do matter. He should set a good example, rather than a blatant disrespect for the
law, and, more importantly, the handicapped citizens of our community. I was hit by a
drunk driver and permanently paralyzed at age 19. My handicapped friends and I rely on
handicapped parking spots to get in and out of our vehicles. In addition, Reynoso’s
employees write $400 citations to anyone else who violates parking in handicapped
parking spaces throughout the City. Reynoso should be ashamed. Reynoso supposedly
does not work at AIS anymore but maybe he can tell his AIS friends not to park their
personal vehicles and work vehicles in their one and only handicapped parking stall.

Vivian Sandoval – Good evening Madam Mayor and city council, my name is Cecilia and
I have been a resident of the City of El Monte for the past 17 years and currently raising
my family as well. We decided to get involved in our community several years ago. It’s
quite disappointing to see the conflicts happening in our city. I started looking at other
cities and BOY! they sure put us to shame. As well as the high school district, they too
seem to have conflicts of their own. As a mother of 3 girls, I wanted them to look up to
someone in their community that truly cares. When we first saw Mayor Ancona’s
campaign, we knew we were headed in the right direction and so did my girls. We ask that
the community support our new Mayor and we also ask the former administration to step
aside and move on. P.S. Just like our new streetlights we are headed in a Brighter future.

Teresa Sandoval – I would like to start off by saying that it is clearly noted that the old
administration has trouble letting go. It is also clear that they prefer power over community.
With the recent attacks on the former chief of police and our current Mayor is just plain
childish. Why can we stay focused on how we can improve our city and our parks, hence
Zamora Park. My family and I have been living here for almost 25 years, never have I
seen such disrespect to the women in leadership. Article upon articles about how bad El
Monte is doing. WAKE up! Looks like the old administration has some issues and for that
reason they lost on November 3rd. Mayor Ancona, Councilmembers Martinez, Morales,
and Puente make the residents believe that you too care about this community and why

  4
   City Council Meeting Minutes of June 16, 2021

we voted you in. Continue to lead Madam Mayor because I too cannot stand distractions
such as pests.

Anonymous – I have been an El Monte City Employee for many years. Things have
changed and many of us don’t look forward to going to work anymore. Things are getting
worse by the day and I would fear for my job if administration knew that I wrote this letter
of concern. That is why I must remain anonymous. I am told that the City might bring in
a private investigator to check into information that leaked from City Hall East. The
information that leaked is probably truthful but being honest isn’t respected here anymore.
As long as the investigator is going to investigate nonsense, why don’t they also look into
things that matter. For example, Councilmember Morales personal escort in a police
vehicle by Police Officers Lune and Rojas, to Greater El Monte Hospital for her Covid-19
vaccination shot. This incident was witnessed by many El Monte City employees who
observed this incident. Both Morales and Police Chief Reynoso lied and denied what
actually happened that day. Regarding Chief Reynoso, his unethical and perhaps illegal
actions to procure the project roomkey contract was swept under the carpet. This cost the
City $150,000 because of his corruption. Prior to gaining the contract, City Manager Alma
Martinez was asked by Councilmember Victoria Martinez how the bidding process was
conducted. Our City Manager replied that it was fair and above board. When asked to
explain further she said she would report later. She was then asked if any City employees
worked for the private security company AIS. She replied, “only one but that employee
wasn’t involved.” Wasn’t involved? Chief Reynoso made the final selection! Somebody is
not telling the truth. It should be known that Reynoso and Sgt. Luna obtain bids for security
purposes for project roomkey. Luna obtained (2) bids and told both companies that their
bids would be submitted to Chief Reynoso who would select the most qualified company.
It was never disclosed that Reynoso’s company was also competing. Of course, Chief
Reynoso selected his own company. This information was subsequently leaked and AIS
was pulled from the contract. Reynoso was disciplined by the City Manager for unethical
behavior and told that he couldn’t work for AIS anymore. In any other City, Reynoso would
have been fired for his actions. Even though Reynoso is supposedly no longer employed
by AIS, I am told that AIS still provides rent free housing and a vehicle for him. Why is
this allowed? How can Chief Reynoso discipline his own employees after what he has
done? I feel that a lot of things need to be investigated but it doesn’t matter because I am
sure Councilmembers Morales, Herrera and Puente will not do the right thing. That’s okay.
We are only 1 ½ years away from the next election. The voters will know the truth about
what is happening in El Monte and vote appropriately.

Sandra Gonzalez – I would like to express my dissatisfaction and disappointment over the
actions of City Manager Alma Martinez. We’ve seen her abuse her power and neglect her
responsibilities time and time again. She is never working at City Hall, residents call and
she cannot be contacted, she takes long extended lunches all around the San Gabriel
Valley and even out to downtown Los Angeles, and she’s been seen taking her directors
to meet with contractors who will be awarded bids. It has gotten to the point where her
negligence has gained news coverage. Facilitating the collusion between Chief Reynoso
and the Absolute International Security contract bid is just the most public of her attempts
to influence the City in favor of her people. As we’ll see during tonight’s meeting, her so-
called “mistake,” with the AIS contract will be billed to the City’s general fund. How much
money will the City have to throw away before realizing the harm Alma Martinez is doing
to us? It’s obvious that she spends her work hours schmoozing with elected officials and
contractors to identify the next city she’ll target because her time in El Monte is coming to

  5
   City Council Meeting Minutes of June 16, 2021

an end. I strongly urge the Mayor and City Council to consider the detriment El Monte will
suffer with Alma Martinez in power.

John Sanchez – I speak on behalf of many residents who are similarly tired of seeing El
Monte’s reputation sink lower and lower with each passing week. Whereas I could once
take pride in being an El Monte citizen, I am disheartened and shamed each time I see
taxpayer dollars go toward patching up the actions of self-serving bureaucrats. The
discussion tonight regarding City Manager Martinez’s influencing the AIS bid is an insult
to the many people El Monte employs who dutifully serve our city for the wellbeing of its
residents. However, it seems that it is just another addition to the pile of corruption
allegations that is weighing down our government and will bring us crashing to the ground.
To be overpaid and irresponsible is one problem, but Alma Martinez directly debases both
the City’s reputation and its ability to function. We need a City Manager who works for our
city, not steals tax payer dollars by never being at work and cares only about cutting
checks for her friends. I have seen other residents take a stand against corruption in El
Monte, and I would hope the Mayor and City Council to do the same.

A S - Mayor Ancona, we the resident's employers of El Monte are concerned because the
city has had so much turmoil in the little time you have been mayor. We blame this on
your lack of leadership, your inability to lead a city and lack of overall knowledge when it
comes to being a mayor. Your agenda items are a joke and shows your lack of
intelligence. Cities must have a process to get city business done; this is something you
have yet to learn. You spreading lies about city staff are going to end up hurting this city
and its residents. Lying to you and to your partner, the Mayor Pro Tem, is like breathing
to the rest of us - you must do it to survive. We are still waiting for you to denounce the
homophobic bigot Kenny Weldon and you along with Mayor Pro Tem Martinez agree to
return all his dirty campaign contributions. A recent article said you are claiming a hostile
work environment with your previous employer. The article also claimed that you had an
affair with a married man as part of your employment - don't ever accuse others of being
unethical. This is ironic since it appears you are causing a hostile work environment with
the City of El Monte and its employees. My advice to you is to learn your duties as the
mayor and stick to them. Oh, and please do not ever call a member of this city a PEST -
this shows your lack of class.

Danielle Zamora – I am a Program Specialist with active San Gabriel Valley, over the past
eight months, we've been working on the clean mobility assessment project within the
cities of El Monte and South El Monte. I would just like to take this opportunity to share an
overview of our findings and recommendations. Through the assessment we collected
input from residents and their travel behaviors and preferences for future transportation
enhancements with the goals of assessment support adoption of cleaner forms of mobility.
This project was funded by California climate investments, a statewide initiative that puts
billions of cap and trade dollars to work, reducing greenhouse gas emissions, safety, the
economy and improving public health and the environment, particularly in disadvantaged
communities. Active SGV collected 259 resident surveys and interviewed 49 community
members. We asked residents how they travel and found that 86% drive alone or with
others. We also learned that 64% of folks walked or rolled to their destinations. We asked
folks which transportation options they would consider using post COVID-19 if readily
available and affordable 73% of respondents would consider using an electric car share
program. This was followed by 68% who would use a shuttle service 60% who would use
public transit and 35% who would use Bike Share. We also learned that 45% of
respondents are interested in a monthly rental program for electric bikes and 40% are

  6
   City Council Meeting Minutes of June 16, 2021

interested in a monthly electric car rental program. So based on the survey and interviews,
we recommend the following ways to support clean mobility, better bus service with more
frequent headways well lighted and shaded stops and safety ambassadors or staff,
cleaner, safer streets that protect with protected bike and roadways, street trees, energy
efficient lighting and ample shade, improved access to an awareness of affordable forms
of public transit and E-mobility, including sharing programs for electric vehicles, bikes, and
other forms of zero emission mobility. To assist with implementation of community
recommendations, it would be helpful to do a pricing analysis for E-micro mobility
programs to help inform a more effective program, especially considering the price
sensitivity of folks within high need communities. Additional information about specific
types of E-bikes residents are interested in renting or buying such as electric cargo bikes,
commuter community bikes or tricycles could also help avoid large upfront investments
that do not best serve the needs and interests of the community. We will have a final report
available for the public to view next month and that can be accessed by visiting
activesgv.org/mobility4EMSEM and if you have any questions about the study, you can
also reach out to me by email, danielle@activesgv.org.

Eva Stoltz – I think you all got a print out from me and that is the rules that re published
by the City of El Monte on all of the vendors that we have out there so why are people
being paid to drive and distribute this if they are not going to be enforced. It is apparent
that no one cares on the Council about the trashing of our City but since we are paying
you you have to listen somewhere on Facebook I saw three places advertising where they
were at so now they are advertising. One place was not only selling food but they were
also having a yard sale which is illegal but no one cares. Now we are turning motels into
homeless units are they going to have rules and who are going to enforce them? The
same ones that are turning a blind eye to what our City is becoming. I don’t envy your job
but you wanted it so do what you were elected to do. It seems as though those who don’t
care what El Monte looks like don’t even live here but they sure like the salaries we pay
them. Like I said before I hear about committees, renters and homelessness not what is
being done for the majority of us. Another thought has been crossing my mind lately about
restaurants not wanting to come to El Monte they do not want to compete with all these
taco stands and food stands on every corner who pay no rents, permits, licenses, taxes
and so forth. I also don’t see any fireworks being taken care of we are hearing bombs
every single night and this has been almost since last year somebody is laughing at their
sleeves at the threat of fines if you do whatever you want to do come to El Monte.

Charles Hoffman – At the last meeting there was talk about maybe someday putting a
façade on the front of the buildings on Main Street. I do understand that there are people
who work for the City and who are on this Council that do not know what businesses and
homes have been on Main Street in the last 167 years plus. Facades of these buildings
and homes have changed over that time on Main Street. A picture was shown of how
Clothes Happy Fashions was used to show what could be done for the front of the façade
on Main Street it was not mentioned that that building once housed the first national bank
of El Monte which opened in 1903 and for 32 years printed national security notes of the
United States of America over $683,000 in that time. I trust one will look more into more
than just the façade of these buildings and also into their history so one can learn more
about the history of El Monte. There are those in the City that need to come to the El
Monte Museum with an open mind and learn about some of the history this City holds but
for whatever reasons do not.

  7
   City Council Meeting Minutes of June 16, 2021

Mike Gomez – Tonight I would like to address, Mayor Ancona’s comments at the end of
the last Council meeting, where she called someone a pest for submitting public comment
cards on items on the agenda that someone was not only an El Monte resident but our
former mayor for 10 years Andre Quintero. Her behavior was totally unacceptable. I quote
Mayor Ancona from that meeting hat “goes to show quite frankly what a pest you can be
and soon after that she says, quite pathetic.” I believe that her comments were out of line
and disrespectful, not just to our former mayor Andre Quintero, but to the whole El Monte
community, and all of El Monte residents who have the right to make public comments at
City Council meetings during the public comment section and on any agendized item. I
remind Mayor Ancona, and the Council that according to Government Code Section
54954.2, “regular meetings must allow public comment on every agenda item, and items
not on the agenda.” I believe a legislative body in this case, this City Council cannot
prohibit criticism, or prevent speech based on content First Amendment protects the
speech. I also quote the publication Open and Public Number Four a Guide to the Ralph
M. Brown Act, League of California Cities under the heading the publics place on the
agenda “every agenda for a regular meeting must allow members of the public to speak
on any item of interest, so long as the item is within the subject matter jurisdiction of the
legislative body further, the public must be allowed to speak on a specific item of business
before or during the legislative bodies consideration of it.” This is a democracy that we live
in and not a dictatorship. Mayor Ancona’s actions and comments here were in my opinion
a form of and intimidation of an El Monte resident and should never be allowed. I think an
apology by Mayor Ancona to our El Monte City and our residents is in order, and especially
to our former mayor Andre Quintero. If that does not happen I think Mayor Ancona should
be censured by the City Council. Thank you.

Rodolfo – I am not a resident of El Monte but to add to what the gentleman just said of
course the residents of El Monte have the right to make a public comment but of course
any member of the public can do that so I welcome anyone to come up. But I wanted to
come here to your Council tonight because I saw something on social media that bothered
me. Especially coming down from the 605 in the City of Downey and over there we have
been trying to figure out what an organization is all about over there they are called the
Downey Leadership Council and they do all of these political attacks sometimes even on
non-politicians which is troubling and illegal but then I found that there is something called
the El Monte Leadership Council and I thought that is interesting and if you look at their
social media and they are pretty similar and it is just striking so you wonder, I implore
especially the residents in El Monte like us in Downey look into what is going on there I
actually call on the Mayor and Mayor Pro Tem to initiate an investigation into who is behind
this entity that is doing illegal actions like attacking private citizens it is completely
unacceptable but of course we are now well aware that there are is a bunch of corruption
going on we heard from the public in the written comments that there are all these
allegations and there have been a lot of allegations about other organizations and just
when I found that from the El Monte Leadership Council then I found something about the
Promise Foundation and there are all sorts of allegations around that claiming that some
of you have taken money that should be going to scholarships for college education that
you have actually been using on your campaign so that is the allegation that is out there
and that is very troubling on multiple levels. So, I call on the Mayor and the Mayor Pro
Tem and the City Council to initiate an investigation into both of these issues so that we
don’t have such a ridiculous unethical waste of money that obviously should be going to
help the community.

  8
   City Council Meeting Minutes of June 16, 2021

Irma Zamorano – I want to thank Mayor Ancona for stepping up and calling Andre
Quintero, he is a bully, he is not a pest, he is a bully. He’s come to many meetings and
tried to get recommendations for eleven years he should of taken the recommendations
and done something about it and move our City forward. During the pandemic he tried to
censor the community I don’t know what Mike Gomez is talking about but he tried to censor
the community. He tried [inaudible] including myself I received two cease and desist
letters one from Andre Quintero and one from Jerry Velasco. Elective officials trying to
sue the public come on he is a lawyer he should know better. So, Mayor thank you for
calling Andre Quintero he is a bully he continues to bully women on this dais and it is
wrong. Andre Quintero has lined his pocket; got paid to play; covered up Councilmember
Jerry Velasco felony drunk driving, insurance fraud, sexual harassment. You know why
does Andre Quintero still show up he was ousted 65 percent of the community ousted him
he is a dictator and we don’t want him here anymore.

David Siegrist – I would like to begin by asking that someone has to audit our
communications system because most of the speakers tonight are so muffled you can’t
understand what they are saying and why people are wearing a mask while they are at
the microphone doesn’t make any sense to me so we really have to have a sound engineer
look at that. First of all, I would like to congratulate the Mayor, the Council and the staff
who put together this marvelous Memorial Day Celebration I have ever attended and I
have been to 25 of them. Congratulations it was beautiful and do it again. I would like to
announce to everybody that the El Monte Library is now open from Monday to Saturday
and behind the El Monte Library you will find free lunch paid for by [inaudible] serving to
the age of 18 and it will be available Tuesday to Friday from 12:00 pm to 1:00pm you do
not have to have your children in the car as long say you have children they will give you
the lunches for the children for free. Now the thing that I am really concerned about is the
Sister City Commission that no longer exist. When I was on it with a number of local
people including Mike Gomez, Irma Zamorano, and others and my wife Estella Torres de
Siegrist we had $4,000 in the account for the Sister Cities Commission and the money
came from what we did selling fireworks on the 4th of July. I would like to see what
happened to the money and also revive the Sister Cities Commission that is a status
symbol for your city. I once had a very good contact for South Korea who wanted to move
his factory to El Monte but the condition was you have to have a sister city of South Korea.
I met another person from Germany who said he would like to start a company here and
hire local people so please consider bring back the Sister Cities Commission. Finally,
happy Flag Day. Flag Day was celebrated in the United States since the year 1916 I wish
that our City would include more ethnicity recognition for example June this is the month
for Jewish Americans Heritage. We missed the Irish American and the Greek American
they were back in March. We missed the Italian American back in October as well as the
German American. I would like to see the Old American’s month that happened back in
May so please consider including all ethnicities, all groups that is what diversity is all about.
I am tired of hearing about all these accusations against people. Military I served for six
years in the military Army, Navy, Marines it was against the law the uniform code of military
justice to start a rumor please people stop these false accusations you ruin reputations
that way so anyway I am to be an El Montian I will stay here I love this community. So,
thank you again for that Memorial Day it was memorable.

Julio Ramirez – I want to direct myself as to my first amendment written communications
there was a certain guy disrespectful for the women here in El Monte. I’ve had enough of
you, I run the City, I do whatever I want. Every time for three years he would do it he did
it before with a City Councilmember, he did it before disrespect the women, talk behind

  9
   City Council Meeting Minutes of June 16, 2021

the women. I come from a mother we all come from a mother we have to respect but he
wasn’t respectful at the last meeting. The Mayor gave him a chance to speak at public
comments. If we all come to the meetings and I have been coming to the meetings and I
have had enough we are gone, he would stand up and say three votes you are out we are
out of here he would do it. We want to start talking about women about the reputation let’s
grow up, let’s grow up. I have seen it in the other City of Baldwin Park, I have seen it in
other cities the way they disrespect the women and that ain’t right he was the Mayor for
eleven years I do it my way out the highway. When we come right here to speak we have
the first amendment but what would he say you are out of line. Let’s grow up and he better
grow up if he lost he lost get on with it you have the command right here. You too and the
vote let’s wake up.

The Mayor was participating via zoom but has now joined the meeting on the dais.

Jane Myring – I am not here to complain this is going to be a lot better. I am so glad that
Covid has somewhat ceased so I am on the El Monte Women’s Club and what we do is
help others we give money to places like pets and everything and we give out scholarships
